_readme: Retrieval ground truth, triaged from the 25 drafted cases.
THE RULE: if you cannot write a specific page id in relevant_page_ids, the case
cannot be scored and does not belong here. 'Relevant Confluence documentation' is
not ground truth — it is an intention. Replace every PLACEHOLDER below with a real
id from your seeded sandbox before running this.
Cases removed from retrieval eval and moved elsewhere (see _engine_cases and
_agent_cases): these are answered by a JQL query or the risk engine, not by
searching an index. Scoring them here measures the wrong component and inflates
your recall number with questions retrieval was never asked to answer.

cases.question: What's blocking INS-101?
cases.note: Engine finds the blocker; retrieval supplies the narrative context. Ground truth is the Confluence page, not the ticket.

cases.question: Which epic does INS-107 belong to?
What is the current release plan?
What work is holding up the release?
cases.note: Target pages must not contain the words 'holding up' — otherwise this is a keyword test wearing a semantic label.

cases.question: Is anything waiting on another team before it can move forward?
What security work still needs to be completed before delivery?
For epic O7, which issues are blocking delivery and what does the release plan say about them?
cases.note: Both pages must appear in top-k. A hit on one is a partial answer that will read as complete.

cases.question: What is the status of the Acme work and are there contractual risks?
What changed most recently in the release plan?
cases.note: EXPECTED TO FAIL. Chunks carry no version metadata, so retrieval cannot answer 'most recently'. Keep the case — a known gap you can name beats a gap you discover in front of a client.

cases.question: What has changed since the previous release update?
cases.note: EXPECTED TO FAIL. Needs page version diffing, not similarity search.

cases.question: What's the status of the contract?
cases.note: Retrieval must surface ALL contracts. Whether the agent then asks for clarification is a separate assertion — see _agent_cases.

cases.question: Who approved the Acme security exception?
cases.note: The nastiest case here. The question PRESUPPOSES the exception exists. Both named pages are topically adjacent, so retrieval will want to return them and a model will then invent an approver. This is the one to watch.

cases.question: What was the exact customer revenue generated by Acme last quarter?
What did the Acme customer say during yesterday's meeting?
What is the CEO's personal opinion about the O7 release?
What is our parental leave policy?
cases.note: Topically distant — the easy negative. If this one fails, the score floor is missing entirely.

_engine_cases: Not retrieval. Assert these against evaluate() / a JQL query, in a separate test:
EVAL-002  current status of INS-107        -> field read
EVAL-006  which items are in progress      -> statusCategory query
EVAL-008  which issues are blocked         -> rule_blocked_dependency output
EVAL-009  biggest delivery risks           -> the risk engine IS this answer
EVAL-018  most recently updated issue      -> sort by last_activity_at()
EVAL-003  assignee and summary of INS-101  -> field read
These have exact expected answers, which makes them better tests than anything
in the retrieval set. They just belong in a different harness.
_agent_cases: Behaviour assertions for Day 4, once the agent exists:
EVAL-020  ambiguous contract     -> must ask which contract, not pick one
EVAL-021  presupposed exception  -> must decline, not confabulate an approver
EVAL-023  exact deploy date      -> must decline rather than infer from sprint dates
